submission.natural_language_explanation: This is a retrospective recency-mixing head with a first-token sink: at a text's second token it gives 0.44-0.85 of its attention to the opening token and the rest to itself (0.2-0.4 at the third token, under 0.1 by the sixth), so its write is dominated by the opening token's value there and by the last one to three tokens elsewhere, and it departs from its mean write when those values are unusual. Predict active, at 0.82-1.0 of the scan max (4.4-5.5 above the floor) at the second token and 0.42-0.76 at tokens 3-4, any text that opens with an opening bracket or a curly quote ('(', '[', '{', '(('); active at 0.27-0.57 (1.4-3.1) at the second token for most other capitalised openers - content words, names, quantifiers, question words, prepositions and word-initial fragments ('Cloud', 'Federal', 'NASA', 'First', 'In', 'At', 'Most', 'A', 'An', 'S'+'ierra', 'Carl'+'os', 'Ass'+'essment'), though a few determiners ('Each', 'Her') stay just below; active at 0.27-0.63 inside a parenthesis or square bracket that follows a word ('(IP)', '(which lasted two hours)') and at 0.42-0.50 inside a long decimal digit run of unusual pieces ('4679853458969239'); and inactive at 0.11-0.22 (0.6-1.2) for a text that opens with the capitalised determiner 'The' plus common lowercase words and uses no parenthesis, bracket, curly quote, capitalised word or unusual digit run after the first token; the head's weak zone is bare lowercase openers (0.33) and the other common pronouns and determiners ('It', 'He', 'She', 'We', 'They', 'Our', 'Your', 'Their', 'This', 'Some'), which sit on the line at 0.15-0.29 and cross only when the second word is a heavier content word ('He described' 0.26, 'This book' 0.27) rather than a light one ('He walked' 0.16).

rival_explanations: The head fires at the second token of any text whatever it says - the top examples only look like opening-token classes because documents start with brackets, capitals or digits - so every probe of two or more tokens, including a 'The ...' sentence, is predicted active.

The head fires whenever the previous token is unusual, wherever it sits, so a capitalised name or a rare word in mid-sentence ('... met Sarah ...', '... by William Smith ...') is predicted as active as a text's opening bracket, and being a bracket is incidental.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The morning light fell across the kitchen table and the coffee went cold.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Core inactive class: capitalised 'The' followed only by common lowercase words, with no parenthesis, bracket, curly quote, capitalised word or unusual digit run after the first token, so the hypothesis predicts a peak of only 0.6-1.2.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The old man walked slowly down the road, past the shops, and stopped by the river.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Longer 'The'+lowercase sentence with commas and a second clause, none of which the hypothesis counts as a trigger, so still inactive.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The botanist described a rare quixotic shrub that grows along the southern coast.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Hard negative for a rare lowercase word mid-sentence: the tokens after 'The' are all lowercase pieces (' qu', 'ix', 'otic'), matching none of the hypothesis's named active classes, so it keeps a 'The'+lowercase text inactive while rival 2 predicts the rare word alone fires.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The landlord described the obstreperous tenant in a long letter to the council.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Same test with a different rare lowercase adjective whose tokens are lowercase pieces (' obst', 're', 'per', 'ous'), to see whether previous-token rarity anywhere is enough to fire while the hypothesis says no.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The guard said "nobody enters after dark" and shut the gate.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The quote token is the straight '"' rather than the claimed curly quote, and every token after 'The' is lowercase, so the hypothesis predicts inactive.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The price rose to 42 dollars before the store closed again.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The single two-digit token ' 42' is not the 'long decimal digit run of unusual pieces' the hypothesis names, so this stays in the inactive class.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The meeting ended early; the chairs were stacked against the wall.
adversarial_test_results.detail: A semicolon token and a second clause, all lowercase after the first token: no claimed trigger token, so inactive.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The cloud drifted over the federal building most of the afternoon.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Keeps the trigger words 'cloud', 'federal' and 'most' but only as lowercase mid-sentence tokens, not the capitalised opening tokens the hypothesis names, so it predicts inactive.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The windows cloud over whenever the kettle boils in the kitchen.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Keeps the trigger word 'cloud' but as a lowercase verb token in mid-sentence, a role and position the hypothesis does not treat as activating.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The first car reached the coast at noon and the rest followed later.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Keeps the trigger word 'first' but as a lowercase mid-sentence token rather than the capitalised opening token 'First', so the hypothesis predicts inactive.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The editor said opening brackets should follow a space and never a word.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Same topic as the bracket examples but with only the word 'brackets', no bracket token: the hypothesis fires on the token, not the topic, so inactive.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The parser rejected the file because a curly quote appeared in the wrong place.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Discusses a curly quote but contains no curly quote token and no capitalised token after 'The', so the hypothesis predicts inactive.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Some of the older buildings were torn down last year.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Weak-zone determiner 'Some' followed by the light token ' of', which the hypothesis puts on the line at 0.15-0.29 without crossing.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: They were waiting outside the station when the train arrived.
adversarial_test_results.detail: 'They' with the light auxiliary token ' were' is in the stated weak zone, not a heavier-content-word crossing.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: It was already late when the shop finally closed its doors.
adversarial_test_results.detail: 'It' followed by the light token ' was' is predicted below the line, unlike an 'It' plus heavy content word case.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: He walked down the lane without saying a word to anyone.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The hypothesis's own non-crossing example: 'He' plus ' walked' at 0.16, a light second token.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: This is the last time the council will meet before the election.
adversarial_test_results.detail: 'This' followed by the light token ' is' is predicted below the line, in contrast to the crossing 'This book' at 0.27.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: We have enough wood to last until the middle of winter.
adversarial_test_results.detail: 'We' with the light token ' have' sits on the line in the 0.15-0.29 weak zone without crossing.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Each of the students received a small notebook and a pencil.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The hypothesis explicitly says the determiner 'Each' stays just below the line, and its second token ' of' is light.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Her voice carried across the empty hall and everyone turned around.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The hypothesis explicitly says the determiner 'Her' stays just below the line and names no crossing condition for it.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: (Update) The bridge will close for repairs next Monday morning.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Opens with the claimed bracket token '(' so the hypothesis predicts 0.82-1.0 of the scan max at the second token 'Update'.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: [Draft] All visitors must sign in at the front desk before entering.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Opens with the claimed opening bracket '[' rather than '(', testing that the bracket class is not specific to round brackets.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: “Quiet,” she said, and closed the door behind her.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Opens with the curly quote token '“' that the hypothesis lists among its strongest openers, with the second token 'Qu'.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The laboratory (lab) moved to a new building last spring.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The bracket token ' (' follows the word ' laboratory', the position in which the hypothesis predicts active at 0.27-0.63, despite the 'The' opener.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: (La casa) estaba vacía cuando llegamos al pueblo.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Same opening-bracket token mechanism in Spanish, testing the token-level claim in a language other than the examples' English.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Cloud storage costs have fallen sharply over the past decade.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The opening token is the capitalised content-word fragment 'Cloud', one of the hypothesis's named activating tokens, predicted active at the second token (0.27-0.57).

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Assessment results will be published at the end of the term.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The opening tokens are exactly the claimed word-initial fragments 'Ass'+'essment', predicted active at the second token.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Most of the guests had already left when the band started.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The opening token is the capitalised quantifier 'Most', predicted active at 0.27-0.57, while rival 2 reading only previous-token rarity treats 'Most' as common and predicts inactive.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The invoice listed 8723491055637142 units shipped last month.
adversarial_test_results.detail: A long decimal digit run of unusual pieces, tokenised as seven digit tokens in mid-sentence, which the hypothesis predicts active at 0.42-0.50, with a different digit string from the example.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: He described the procedure in careful detail for the new staff.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Weak pronoun 'He' with the heavier content token ' described', the hypothesis's crossing example at 0.26, while rival 2 treats 'described' as unremarkable and predicts inactive.
